tagline: Out of Apache to granite mountains half a billion years old.
intro: From Apache the byway runs west on Highway 19 and then branches, north on Highway 58 to Carnegie and on to Mountain View, south to Medicine Park, across rocky lowlands, mixed-grass prairie and cross timbers. Highway 49 carries it on west through the Wichita Mountains Wildlife Refuge.

The refuge has been kept since 1901, the oldest in the Fish and Wildlife Service system, on mountains about 500 million years old. The bison, elk and longhorn cattle on its prairies were all brought in after it opened, the elk from Jackson Hole in 1911.

moments.title: Meers
moments.text: Of the 1901 gold camp only the store remains. It served as the post office until 1989, and in 1985 the Oklahoma Geological Survey put a seismograph in it.

moments.title: Mount Scott
moments.text: A three-mile paved road climbs to the 2,464-foot top. Artillery fire from Fort Sill nearby is often heard across the refuge and sometimes taken for thunder.

moments.title: Medicine Park
moments.text: Many of its old buildings are the Wichitas' own red granite cobblestones, but the resort began in 1908 as a surplus Army tent serving hot meals by a dammed swimming hole.
